title: Income and wealth concentration, 2022–23
finding: Estimates the top 1% received 22.6% of national income and held 40.1% of wealth in 2022–23.
official: Consumption-based poverty estimates and distributional measures are not the same quantities as pre-tax income or wealth shares.
reconciliation: Both a fall in measured consumption poverty and high income/wealth concentration can coexist. Compare definitions, reference years and modelling assumptions; do not subtract one measure from another.

title: Improving headline labour indicators versus quality of employment
source: ILO and Institute for Human Development
kind: Independent interpretation of official survey microdata
finding: 2024 employment report characterises recent improvements in labour indicators as paradoxical, emphasising the quality and structure of available jobs.
official: PLFS unemployment and labour participation rates describe specific survey definitions, not adequate pay or job security.
reconciliation: PLFS headline improvement is not disproved by the ILO/IHD report: the report uses official labour surveys but raises distinct quality and youth-employment concerns. Not statistically independent primary collection.

title: Youth employment and skills mismatch
source: ILO and Institute for Human Development
kind: Independent expert research using official microdata
finding: Investigates educated youth labour-market outcomes and skills mismatch over two decades.
official: Aggregate unemployment rates can mask age and educational differences.
reconciliation: Compare youth-specific and education-specific denominators rather than projecting all-age unemployment results onto young graduates.

title: Internet shutdowns: 2023 versus 2024
finding: Documented at least 116 shutdowns in India in 2023 and 84 in 2024.
official: An event-monitoring count is not identical to the number of formal government orders. Attribution to Union versus state authorities must be recorded separately.
reconciliation: The independently recorded count decreased between the two years, but remained substantial. It alone cannot measure all civil liberties or the motives of each order.

title: Electoral bonds: judicial finding
kind: Judicial primary record (not independent statistical study)
finding: Supreme Court order records the February 2024 holding that electoral-bond nondisclosure violated citizens’ right to information and the unlimited corporate donation amendment was arbitrary.
official: The scheme was enacted as a policy mechanism; implementation itself did not establish constitutional compliance.
reconciliation: A court holding establishes a specific legal conclusion, not a quantitative measure of the overall health of democracy or proof of individual corrupt conduct.

title: Political finance and electoral-bond transparency
finding: The Court ordered disclosure of electoral-bond purchasing and redemption data after the February 2024 judgment.
official: Claims that electoral bonds improved transparency must distinguish anonymous issuance from eventual court-ordered disclosures.
reconciliation: Records establish a constitutional transparency failure under the judgment; they do not alone determine motives of donors or recipients.
